Only one person can get Child Benefit for a child, and there's no limit to how many children you can claim for. By claiming you can get: an allowance paid for each child (usually every 4 weeks); National Insurance credits counting towards your State Pension; and a National Insurance number for your child (usually before they turn 16). Even if you choose not to receive the payments, you should still claim to get the other advantages. You get NI credits automatically if you claim and your child is under 12; if you don't need them, your partner can apply to transfer them, or another carer can apply for Specified Adult Childcare credits. You must report any change of circumstances to the Child Benefit Office.

ELIGIBILITY (Who can get Child Benefit): Only one person can get Child Benefit for a child. You normally qualify if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK. You're usually responsible if you live with them, or you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or equivalent in kind) towards looking after them. Rules differ if your child goes into hospital/care or lives with someone else. For children 16+: you normally still qualify if under 20 and in approved education or training (you can apply to continue 20 weeks if a 16/17-year-old leaves education and registers with a careers service or the armed services). Fostering: you get it as long as the council isn't paying towards accommodation/maintenance. Adopting: you can claim as soon as the child comes to live with you. Two people cannot get it for the same child — if you can't agree, HMRC decides. Eligibility can also apply if living abroad/Crown servant; settled status lets you claim; pre-settled status rules depend on working, jobseeking, sufficient resources, studying, or being a family member of an EEA/Swiss national. You stop getting it if your child starts paid work 24+ hours a week (and is no longer in approved education/training), starts an apprenticeship in England, or starts getting certain benefits.

HOW TO CLAIM: You can claim 48 hours after registering the birth, or once a child comes to live with you, and it can be backdated up to 3 months from the claim date. Only one person can claim per child, so decide who should claim (the claimant gets the NI credits; you and your partner can claim for different children).
